title: When the gym removes a member, the member's desk photo and body measurements stay on the server with no end
what: The gym removes a member by marking them deleted on its list. Nothing then deletes that member's photo taken at the desk or the body measurements the trainer saved. Saving new ones is refused for a removed member, but the old photo and measurements stay until the whole gym is deleted. Body measurements are health data. The privacy notice says the gym's records about a member are kept as long as the gym keeps them, and the gym thinks it no longer keeps this member.
expected: Removing a member also removes their desk photo and body measurements (or after a short, stated time to allow undo), and the notice says how long they stay.
who: members a gym removes from its list
how_often: every removed member who had a desk photo or measurements
fix_line: When a member is removed for good, delete their desk photo and measurements too, and state the time in the notice.

title: Trainer questions, trainer summaries and sent workout reports are only deleted when someone opens them again
what: The privacy notice promises questions to a trainer go after 180 days, the trainer summary after 90 days with no update, and a sent workout report after 30 days. No timed job does any of this: the nightly clean-up never touches these three. Each is removed only when the member or someone at that gym next opens that list. If a gym stops using the feature, or the member stops opening the app, the old questions, workout summaries and report files stay on the server. Member messages to the gym have the same gap (already written down separately).
expected: These are deleted on a schedule at the promised time, whoever opens the app.
who: members who asked a trainer, shared a summary or sent a workout report
how_often: whenever the gym or member stops opening that list
fix_line: Add these three deletions to the nightly clean-up.

items.reason: 6 promises read. P-A7-panel-3-21: the server keeps only check-in dates and trusts the phone for the 20 minutes and 6 sets; that is a deliberate privacy choice (only dates leave the phone, after consent) and breaks no privacy promise. P-A7-panel-3-29: personal messages are WhatsApp only, the in-app send is hidden for them. P-A7-panel-3-33 and P-A7-panel-3-22: message and card words, no personal data. P-A7-panel-3-24: the sample products come from the server's demo start, not personal data, count not checked in this lens. P-A7-panel-2-73: the phone's check-in flow is outside this area. No privacy promise found broken.

Notice: the privacy notice and data agreement name the gym as in charge of desk photos, measurements, diet plans, orders and messages, and ask the gym to take a photo only with agreement. Consent: a workout report needs the member's yes; the workout offer logs consent. Deletion: removed members keep photo and measurements (01); timed deletes only run on read (02). Breach timing and children: nothing in this area holds a screen or step for either.

Every read in this area goes through the gym's own key or a staff session; the server keeps each gym to its own rows. No MettleUp staff reader is in this area (support access and its read log are HQ, checked in the HQ lens). Trainer summaries refuse a trainer who is not the member's trainer; the desk without the trainer tick is refused. The browser keeps the gym key and only counts and times for alerts, never message text.

Kept longer than the notice says: trainer questions, trainer summaries and sent report files (02); messages to the gym already written as FN-A3-help-02. Kept with no end after removal: desk photo and measurements (01). Gym alerts go after 30 days on a timer; staff browser push addresses are removed when dead. Shop orders, plan requests and diet plans are the gym's records kept as long as the gym keeps them, as the notice says.

Outside sends from this area: personal and group WhatsApp messages open the staff's own WhatsApp (the data agreement says the gym is responsible); in-app messages go to members' phones through Google Firebase, named in both notices; alerts to a staff browser go through the browser's push service with the content encrypted; the desk photo travels inside the answer with no link; product photos sit in a public store but hold products only. No AI, analytics, Health Connect, Google Health or Fitbit calls in this area.

A gym delete cascades to photos, measurements, diet plans and report files. A member removed by the gym keeps photo and measurements (01). A member who leaves from the app loses trainer summary and questions at once, but timed deletes only run on read (02). A real delete was not run (live write); nightly backups expire in 7 days per the notice.
